summary: Claude Hagège is a linguist who studied at institutions including the École Normale Supérieure and under André Martinet. He held posts at the University of Poitiers (1970–1987), EPHE (~1977–1988), and Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques worked in Indology, history, and archaeology, studying under George Cœdès (~1958–1969). He served as director at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1965–1973) and taught epigraphy and history at the EPHE (~1970–1997).

Claude Lévi-Strauss studied philosophy and other fields, attending Paris Law Faculty and studying under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the University of São Paulo, EPHE, EHESS, and the Collège de France (chair of Anthropologie sociale, 1959–1982).

Claude-Auguste Court was active in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the École polytechnique and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1812–1813), and served as an Engineer Officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army (~1827–1843).
Claudia Benthien is a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at Washington University in St. Louis (1993–1994) and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~2004).
Claudia Weber is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Claudius Buchanan, a scholar in Indology and religious studies, studied at the University of Glasgow and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795). In 1801, he served as Vice-Provost at Fort William College.

Claus Oetke was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He taught at Hamburg, Kiel, and Vienna, and led the Department of Indology at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

Claus Vogel worked in Indology and Tibetology, completing his PhD and habilitation at the University of Marburg under Friedrich Müller and Wilhelm Rau. He held posts at Marburg, Göttingen, and as Ordinarius at the University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She held posts at the University of Canterbury in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.
Clemente Merlo was a linguist who studied at the University of Pavia (~1898–1903) and held a post at the University of Pisa (~1910–1949).
Clyde Kluckhohn studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at CNRS, University of Lyon, Sorbonne University (1967–1988), and directed the Institut de civilisation indienne (~1980–1993).

Colette Sciberras is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and with traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean studied philosophy and religious studies under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria (both attested 2002).
Colin Turnbull studied at Westminster School (~1938–1942), Magdalen College (~1946–1950), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951), working in Tibetology and other fields.

Collett Cox is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda, as well as in Japan, and served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1999, 2017).

Conor Roddy is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Kathleen M. Higgins (attested 2011), also studying under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.
Conrad Bursian, an archaeologist and historian, studied at Leipzig and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Leipzig, Tübingen, Zurich, Jena, and the University of Munich (~1874–1883).
Conrad M. Arensberg studied at Harvard University (~1928–1934) and held a post at Columbia University (~1953–1979).
